full_judgment:
2. The facts of the case, in brief, are that the respondent, Md. Kandar Molla, the predecessor in interest of respondent Nos. 1(a)-1(i) and Md. Amir Molla, the predecessor in interest of respondent Nos. 2(a)-2(g) as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 89 of 1987 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Manda, Naogaon praying for declaration of title and confirmation of possession over the suit land contending, inter-aria that 0.80 acre land under CS Khatian No.109, Plot No.786 corresponding to hal dag No. 858, corresponding to SA Khatian No. 133 and RS Khatian No. 35 appertaining to Mouza Matgari belonged to Sobhan Sardar as Korfa Tenant under Rayati tenant Hossain Molla. On Chaitra 5, 1332 BS Sobhan Sardar being unable to pay rents surrendered the suit land in favour of Hossain Molla by executing an Istafa Patra. Hossain Molla took Possession of the suit land and transferred the same to Zamir Molla, the predecessor of the plaintiffs, by executing a registered kabala being No. 4665 dated 5-10-1918. Zamir Molla died leaving two sons Amir Molla and Kandar Molla and widow Afzan Bewa. SA khatian No. 133 was duly prepared in their names. During RS operation the field survey (parcha) was prepared in the names of Amir Molla and Kandar Mollah and while the defendants threatened to dispossess Amir Molla and Kandar Molla from the suit land they were constrained to file Other Class Suit No. 312 of 1974 which was renumbered as Other Class Suit No. 20 of 1984 praying for permanent injunction and during pendency of the said suit the defendants on 7-5-87 disclosed that RS Khatian No. 35 for the suit land was prepared in the names of the plaintiffs along with Pakalu Sardar, the predecessor of defendant Nos. 1 to 7, Baul Sardar, the predecessor of defendant Nos. 8 to 11 and Arsi Bewa, the predecessor of defendant Nos. 12 and 14 although none of them had right, title and possession in the suit land and as such, assuming that no fruitful result would come out from Other Class Suit No. 20 of 1984 due to wrong recording of RS Khatian No. 35, the plaintiffs on 19-5-1987 got the suit withdrawn with permission from the Court to sue afresh and being under apprehen-sion of dispossession from the suit land, the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 89 of 1987. 

 3. Defendant Nos. 1 to 14 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all material allegations made in the plaint and contending, inter-alia, that the suit land belonged to Sobhan Sardar, the predecessor of the defendants, who was a Korfa tenant under Hossain Molla at Jama Rs. 3 in CS Khatian No. 109, Plot No. 786, area 0.80 acre. Sobhan Sardar died leaving two sons Pakalu and Baul one daughter Mani and SA Khatian was prepared in the names of Amir Molla and Kandar Molla wrongly and beyond the knowledge of the predecessor in interest of the defendant-appellants, however during RS Khatian No. 35 was prepared in the names of the contesting defendant-appellants along with the names of the plaintiffs for which the predecessor in interest of defendant-appellants filed Objection Case No. 12 of 1967 which was rejected by order dated 5-9-1967 against which Appeal No. 5331 of 1967 was filed by the predecessor in interest of the defendant-appellants and the same was allowed by the order dated 19-8-1968. Kandar Molla and the another filed other Class Suit No. 312 of 1974 in the Court of Munsif at Naogaon for permanent Action in respect of SA Khatian No. 133, Plot No. 786 area 0.80 acre and filed an application for temporary injunction was rejected on 18-12-1974. 

 13. It is admitted by the parties that the suit land belonged to one Sobhan Mollah as Korfa tenant under rayati tenant Hossain Mollah. The present plaintiff-respondents have come with an allegation that Sobhan Sarder surrendered the suit land in favour of Hossain Mollah being unable to pay rent after executing an Istafa Patra. It has been further alleged that after taking over possession Hossain Mollah sold out the suit land in favour of one Zamir Molla who died leaving behind the plaintiffs as his heirs. It has been also alleged that the present plaintiff-respondents as heirs of Zamir Mollah has been possessing the suit land and SA Khatian was prepared duly in the name of the plaintiffs. On the other hand, the contesting defendants denied the contention of the plaintiffs and counter claimed that Sobhan Sarder never surrendered the suit land and never executed any Istafa Patra who as owner in possession died leaving behind the predecessor of the defendant-appellants and the defendants have been possessing the suit land. 

 21. On perusal of the impugned judgment passed by the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division, it appears that he has considered the oral and documentary evidence of the parties and rightly held that the trial Court on assessment of the evidence on record found that the Istafa Patra (Exhibit-4) is a genuine document, and the PWs have successfully proved the Istafa Patra on the basis of which kabala dated 5-10-1918 has been executed by Hossain Mollah in favour of Zamir Mollah whose heirs are the plaintiffs and SA Khatian has been prepared in their names and RS Khatains also prepared in their names in preliminary stage. The learned Judge of the single Bench of the High Court Division further held that since the Istafa Patra was found to be genuine, transfer of the suit land by Hossain Mollah to Zamir Mollah, the predecessor of the plaintiffs by kabala dated 5-10-1918 is also genuine. The learned Judge of Single Bench of the High Court Division also held that the learned Judge of the appellate Court while reversing the judgment passed by the trial Court did not follow the procedure laid down in Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure and thus, the judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court below is not a proper judgment of reversal. Where there is misreading of evidence or non-consideration of material evidence affecting the merit of the case, the High Court Division can review the evidence and correct the error in exercise of its revisional power.
